draft.title: A bipolar world
card: A bipolar world has two main centres of power. After 1945, these were the United States and the Soviet Union, called the superpowers.
a military alliance formed in 1949. The United States and its Western allies promised to defend each other if one was attacked.
a rival military alliance formed in 1955. The Soviet Union led it, together with its allies in Eastern Europe.

The superpowers competed for influence around the world, by backing friendly governments and spreading their ideas. They avoided fighting each other directly, but often supported opposing sides in conflicts elsewhere.
draft.remember: Two superpowers led rival alliances and competed for influence, but did not fight each other directly.

a.q: Why is the world after 1945 described as bipolar?
opts: Two superpowers led rival blocs and held most power
Two wars were fought between the main powers
Two continents were ruled by one government
Two alliances merged into a single organisation
a.why: Bipolar means two main centres of power. The United States and the Soviet Union each led a bloc of allies. The idea of two wars is tempting, but the superpowers avoided fighting each other directly.
a.clue: Think about what bi means, and who held the power.

b.q: In the 1950s, a Soviet-backed government and a US-backed government fought a war in a third country. Their superpowers sent weapons and advisers but did not fight each other. What does this show about the superpowers?
opts: They competed for influence while avoiding direct conflict
They had ended their rivalry and cooperated
They had joined together in one military alliance
They had lost influence over smaller countries
b.why: Each superpower backed one side to gain influence, but neither fought the other directly. Cooperation is wrong because they supported opposing sides. Joining one alliance is wrong because NATO and the Warsaw Pact were rivals.
b.clue: Who was fighting, and who was only supplying help?

a.best: Two superpowers led rival blocs and held most power

b.best: They competed for influence while avoiding direct conflict

check.summary: No problems found. The NATO (1949) and Warsaw Pact (1955) dates are correct, both questions have one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card.
